labels.notes: Unmarked, partial, and the REPORT discloses this correctly. Conclusion: ghd_02_19.tex:1104-1106 says 'any other GHD u : U satisfies U ⊆ U1 and thus also u1|U = u', and the Lean gives `∀ U₂ u₂, IsDevelopment … → U₂ ≤ U₁ ∧ EqOn u₁ u₂ U₂` (ers_theorem_4_82_solution) plus 'the unique MGHD' (_unique, every IsMaximalDevelopment equals U₁). Lean ≥ paper on these hypotheses: hmax (l. 117 maximality, implied by l. 1094), honesided (OneSidedBoundary, implied by (4.83)), s₀ ∈ S (in place of S connected). Narrower than the paper on these, each disclosed in the checklist, SCOPE and REPORT: the abstract equation with SolutionLocal, SolutionsGlue and the new SolutionRestricts; a GHD read 'S Cauchy' (DEC-162); the GH side conditions on each development (as in ers_theorem_4_82_of_sliceRestart, which the target allows); hagree (Rem 4.67's variation, a named hypothesis as the target allows, derived from Thm 4.64 for (U₁, A) in _of_ers_theorem_4_64 and _secondCountable through local_uniqueness's existential, frontier_stays_in, slice_restart with 4.64's Q, and hacausal); hstep = slice_restart with Q = GluedRestartAt (Steps 3-4 and 'u3 is a GHD', :1135-1138). Every hypothesis is one of: a ladder property read on a development, an [[edge_hypothesis]] id of programme/ladder.toml (slice_restart, one_sided_boundary, frontier_stays_in, local_uniqueness), the abstract-equation vocabulary, or the named agreement. The witness satisfies every hypothesis of every form, so none is vacuous. The curation proposal (seven decls, extra_lean_files, partial and bucket B unchanged) is honest about the narrowing. One exception is the curation notes wording (finding 7).

by: Causal.ers_theorem_4_82_restart (Ers482Solution.lean:227): the restart step at any development. Its instance at the non-maximal ]-1/2,1/2[ against ]-1,1[ is Causal.Ers482Witness.timelikeLine_ers_theorem_4_82_restart (:883). There the SliceRestart premise (p = ±1/2 ∈ ∂A ∩ U₂, spacelike in U₂) and GluedRestartAt's premise (V = ]-1,1[, V ∩ U₁ ⊆ A) are met (restart_exercised, :697), so Q has to be proved (sliceRestart_halfIoo, :870, through restarts82). The result is a strictly larger development. At that pair the restart holds while U₂ ≤ U₁ fails (three_quarters_*), so the per-pair restart is not the per-pair inclusion, and this is proved in Lean.
Causal.ers_theorem_4_82_solution_of_restarts (:539): its uniform hrestart holds at every pair of the witness (restarts82, :835), and that is not vacuous at the non-maximal pair.
acceptance.not_by: Causal.ers_theorem_4_82_solution and its siblings _unique, _of_globallyHyperbolicOn, _of_ers_theorem_4_64 and _secondCountable. Given the other hypotheses, their hstep is equivalent to the conclusion (ers_theorem_4_82_solution_hstep_iff, :509). This is necessary for the fixed-U₁ shape that the target title asks for, and it is disclosed. See findings 1 and 2.
acceptance.geometric_Q: GluedRestartAt (:160) says: for every neighbourhood V ⊆ U₂ of p with V ∩ U₁ ⊆ A, there is an open O ⊆ V, not inside U₁, such that S is a Cauchy surface of U₁ ⊔ O for cau of the glued function. It names no sol and no maximality. The solving part and the strict enlargement are derived in ers_theorem_4_82_restart. It is not the old Q in disguise: the old Q '∃ j, dom i₀ < dom j' was met at a non-maximal base by j = i₁ with no geometry, while this Q needs an O inside every small V around p. It carries only the Cauchy half of 'U₁ ∪ O is a GHD', which is ERS's own 'it is easy to see' (:1138), so it belongs with slice_restart's supplier. It is satisfiable non-trivially (restarts82, O = ]p-ε, p+ε[), but only with one causality and one solution, so on the line its Cauchy part reduces to the interval fact (disclosed). The dispatch's 'O ∋ p' is the stronger hypothesis. It implies this Q (GluedRestartAt.of_mem, sliceRestart_gluedRestartAt_of_mem), and the choice is recorded as a question.

Closer's paper findings: (1) l. 1094 vs l. 117 is correct but leaves out ERS's own reconciliation at :1094 (finding 6). (2) (4.83) is applied at the second q ∈ Σ ∩ ∂A (:1135-1137), not at p: correct. The Lean applies one-sidedness at p and quantifies Q over V around p, which is a sound reorganisation because V' ⊆ V keeps V' ∩ U₁ ⊆ A and q ∉ U₁. (3) Restriction of solutions is used at :1138: correct. (4) 'S connected implicit' is imprecise, because :814 makes it explicit (finding 5). Also correct: ers_remark_4_78 needs subluminality (hsub, hm, hmacausal; Causal/ErsMughd.lean:271), and the dispatch's Causal.Causality.ers_theorem_4_79 is really Causal.ers_theorem_4_79.

No author-level reading is presented as settled. S connected and l. 117 are stated as findings, where the Lean assumes less (see the wording fixes in findings 5 and 6).

findings.what: The main theorem ers_theorem_4_82_solution and every sibling except _of_restarts still have the defect the target exists to cure. Given the rest, their hstep is equivalent to the conclusion (proved by the closer, _hstep_iff), so the witness can only discharge it vacuously (hstep_of_le). This is unavoidable for the fixed-U₁ shape the target title asks for, and it is disclosed in SCOPE, REPORT and the binder note. The acceptance is met elsewhere: by ers_theorem_4_82_restart with its non-maximal instance, and by _of_restarts with restarts82. But the proposals lead with the content-free form, and the only is_causal-level keeper entry (entry 1) is that form. _of_restarts exists only with hG/hT (globally_hyperbolic, tarentin), so no is_causal consequence has content.
findings.fix: Make _of_restarts the form of record: list it first in the binder and curation, and put it first in the keeper's entries. Add an is_causal-level uniform form (hcaus, hJm, hJp in place of hG, hT; one line from ers_theorem_4_82_solution with hrestart U₁ u₁) so that the is_causal consequence carries the content. Record entries 1 and 2 as specialisations whose hstep is equivalent to the conclusion, as the existing four 4.82 entries are.

findings.what: _of_restarts is the main form specialised at U₀ = U₁, a one-line proof, so as a theorem it is logically weaker than _of_globallyHyperbolicOn. Its value depends entirely on hrestart not being implied by the conclusion and the other hypotheses. That is argued, not proved (disclosed in SCOPE and what_remains). Lean evidence exists only per pair: at (]-1/2,1/2[, ]-1,1[) the restart holds and U₂ ≤ U₁ fails.
findings.fix: Either add a separating model in Lean (all hypotheses of _of_restarts except hrestart hold, the conclusion holds, hrestart fails, e.g. with a causality making {0} Cauchy in ]-1,1[ but not in ]-1/2,1/2+ε[), or reword 'carries the content' to: 'its hypothesis names no maximal development and is exercised at non-maximal pairs; that the conclusion does not imply it is argued, not proved'.

findings.what: The finding says Thm 4.82 is stated 'with no connectedness of S' and that S connected is 'an implicit hypothesis', citing :1118 and :859. But §4's standing setup at ghd_02_19.tex:814 reads 'Let S ⊆ R^{d+1} be a connected hypersurface of R^{d+1}. Initial data for (4.61) on S consists of …', and Thm 4.82 is stated 'of given initial data' (:1101) in the same section. So S connected is explicit in the paper, not implicit. The Lean is unaffected (s₀ ∈ S suffices; IsPreconnected S only in _secondCountable), but as worded the finding would reach the author as an inaccurate statement about the paper.
findings.fix: Cite :814 and reword to: 'S connected is §4's standing hypothesis (:814). The Lean forms need only s₀ ∈ S, except _secondCountable'. Change the checklist row from 'implicit' to '§4 setup, :814'.

findings.what: The l. 1094 vs l. 117 finding is correct as far as it goes, but it leaves out ERS's own next sentences at :1094: 'Note that by Theorem ThmUnique any such GHD u2 would agree with u1 on U1, and thus it would correspond to an extension of u1 : U1 → R. In other words, a MGHD is a GHD that cannot be extended as a GHD.' So in the paper the two notions coincide, via Thm 4.64 on the connected overlap U₁ (hyperbolic solutions live on connected open sets, :100). l. 117 is weaker only in the abstract reading, where Thm 4.64 is not available.
findings.fix: Quote that sentence and reword 'weaker than l. 1094' to 'formally weaker in the abstract reading; ERS identify the two at :1094 through Thm 4.64'.

findings.what: 'Witness Causal.Ers482Witness: hstep exercised at a non-maximal pair' is ambiguous next to the main form, whose hstep is never exercised (_hstep_iff). The binder note_append states this precisely; the curation note does not.
findings.fix: Say: 'the restart step's hstep (ers_theorem_4_82_restart) and _of_restarts' hrestart are exercised at (]-1/2,1/2[, ]-1,1[); the fixed-U₁ hstep is equivalent to the conclusion given the rest (_hstep_iff)'.

findings.what: The checklist uses '✓ weakened' where kb/0006 and the sibling modules (ErsMughd, ErsUniqueness, ErsWitnesses) use '⚠ weakened'. The GluedRestartAt docstring says 'Pure causal topology: no solution, no maximality', but the predicate takes u₁, u₂ and evaluates cau at the glued function.
